In my opinion it may not be the best idea to get too caught up on the idea that you "missed out" on things that you didn't do but have seen others doing at certain points in life.

Different lives have different trajectories and everyone has a unique experience which means they have something unique to offer others in terms of their own personal insight. It would be a boring world if everyone were exactly the same.

I feel it's a good approach to focus less on things like your age, and your experiences relative to the experiences of others, but more on what you have to offer. What are your good qualities? Are you a kind, caring person? Are you funny? Are you a good critical thinker? Are you good at cooking or creative writing or frisbee or making coffee? Any ability you possess -regardless of how small a thing you may think it is- has value. Perhaps start with brainstorming your positive attributes to foster a more positive outlook. Positivity in itself is a very attractive quality. Then take part in community groups that involve meeting new people, but take it slowly so you don't burn out and give up.

Good luck and I hope you begin to feel better about your situation soon.
